_meta.note: Recorded by Kiro Crew's in-product frame recorder (KIROCREW_ACP_RECORD_FRAMES) while an AcpClient(acp_backend='opencode') session ran, so the spawn, the routing seed on OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT, its read-back and the session array are Crew's own. The capture replaced only the OS sandbox step (the recording host has no sandbox backend), as the pi zero-tool capture did; every other step ran as shipped. `opencode acp` 1.19.1, the Real Adapter Contract lane's pin (test/real_adapters/package.json, npm ci), against a loopback OpenAI-compatible model stub reached through opencode's @ai-sdk/openai-compatible provider, with a throwaway HOME; the stub asks for the tool the prompt names with one tool call and answers the tool result with a fixed reply, so no real model or credential was involved. A member session (key member-probe) on a spec with no tools key: AcpClient appended members.member_dispatch_session_server's kirocrew-dashboard entry to session/new, with its gateway port pointed where nothing listens and the recording shell's own KIROCREW_PORT removed, so no call reached a live gateway. The model's kirocrew-dashboard_session_status call raised session/request_permission, the consumer approved it, and the server answered (it refuses, as it cannot reach a gateway to read the probe key's tool policy): the element is mounted and its tool reachable behind opencode's ask. Reduced through capture_acp_compaction.reduce_frames: 2 configOptions select(s) cut to the one option naming its currentValue: the full list is the provider and model catalog the recording host could reach; 1 available_commands_update/session_info_update frame(s) dropped: they carry the recording host's own command inventory and run id; the session id is replaced with the synthetic opencode-session-1; message id(s) replaced with synthetic msg-N values.
